verses.text: A song. A psalm by the sons of Korah. For the music director, to the tune of “The Suffering of Affliction.” A psalm for reflection by Heman the Ezrahite. LORD, God who saves me, I’ve cried out to you day and night.
Let my prayer reach you. Lean in and hear my cry.
My soul is packed with trouble, and my life is getting close to Sheol.
People count me among those going down to the pit. I’m like someone with no one to help,
left among the dead, like those killed and laid in the grave, whom you no longer remember. They’re cut off from your hand.
You’ve put me in the lowest pit, down in the deepest dark.
Your anger weighs hard on me. You’ve battered me with wave after wave. Selah.
You’ve driven my friends away and made them recoil from me. I’m shut in and can’t get out.
My eyes are worn out from grief. I call to you every day, LORD, with my hands stretched out to you.
Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the spirits of those who’ve died get up and praise you? Selah.
Does anyone tell of your faithful love in the grave or talk about your faithfulness in Destruction?
Are your wonders known in the dark or your righteousness in the land where everyone is forgotten?
But I’m still crying out to you, LORD. In the morning my prayer comes before you.
LORD, why do you turn my soul away? Why do you hide your face from me?
I’ve suffered and come close to death since I was young. Your terrors leave me beside myself.
Your fierce anger has swept over me. Your terrors have cut me off.
They surround me like floodwater all day long. They’ve swallowed me up.
You’ve put my loved ones and friends far from me, and my friends are lost in the dark.
